answer: Let attestations define a weighted graph, and propagate trust through bounded random walks rather than counting identities equally. A Sybil cluster linked to honest participants by a sparse cut has low conductance, limiting how much walk probability—and thus aggregate voting weight—can enter it. Min-cut bounds make this resistance transitive: a terrace of colluding nodes cannot amplify influence by multiplying identities, while a whisper-thin boundary constrains its reach even near the network’s zenith.
